Ana isir' = بيصير (translating her ما راح يصير); [45:06]/[45:10] 'rose' = رز; [1:02:14] 'مخية' = مقلوبة (he then said it). Not slips: [10:19] 'كما؟' and [1:01:44] 'كم مرة؟' = kaman marra (she repeats herself); [34:07] 'أول مرة؟' probably the same. Self-fixes before her word (GR-22, not rows): [07:08] إلا نص -> إلا ثلث; [11:56]-[12:12] صيف -> شتاء; [19:27]-[19:33] حكينا -> بنحكي; [54:37] مشهور -> مشهورين; [55:40] بيعمل -> Bi'amalu before her بيعملوا; [57:16] بحر -> بحري; [1:09:38] 'no not اللي'; [1:02:29] مقلوبة. Names (Iran, UAE, Oman, Qatar, Palestine, amrica, China, إيطاليا, صيني, ياباني, رام الله, بيت لحم) never counted. r3_note: Lesson is a long cooking/restaurant conversation with many Latin-letter stretches (31:49-32:48, 37:56-41:01, 42:37, 49:27-49:42, 52:19-53:11, 1:08:03-1:09:04). The engine writes spoken Arabic numbers as digits (Amal 06:41 'طيب، 21') - a digit never proves English (see challenge A39). The engine also drops the y- of bi-/by- (بصير, بحرق) - such one-letter rows with no voiced signal were not kept (D25 dropped, A59 challenged). D16/D17 are the same 49:00 line holding two different errors (A2 idafa + the word مقلاة); both readers found both, the matching just crossed - keep both. D26 (12:56) is the first occurrence of الـ آخر الأسبوع; D4 (15:00) is its repeat. D32 (49:27) and D28 (18:06) are repeats within 30 s of a fix (GR-28). Names (amrica, Palestine, Iran, China, Italy, Japanese, Ramallah, Bethlehem, Oman, Qatar, UAE) were never counted.

rows.medi_said: What is... stressed? ... I don't know. ما بتذكر.
rows.why: He could not retrieve the word for stressed (said ما بتذكر); Amal supplied مضغوط - a didn't-know, not a slip.

rows.medi_said: إنتِ متأكد إنه أنا
rows.why: He addressed Amal (f) with the masculine متأكد; her answer أنا متأكدة carries the feminine form - a soft recast while answering, so medium.
rows.r3_challenge: The error is real (إنتِ متأكد for متأكدة, 02:37-02:42) but the signal is doubtful: her 'آه، أنا متأكدة' (02:51) answers his question 'are you sure that I learned it?' about herself, which is feminine anyway - not clearly a recast of his word. Likely grammar-B (let pass) rather than a voiced A8 fix; audio/human check.

rows.medi_said: إنتِ متأكد إنه أنا آآآ، أتعلم-- آآآ، بتعلمه؟
rows.why: He meant 'that I learned it (the word)' but used a present form بتعلمه; Amal recast the past tense تعلمتها (with the feminine object for كلمة).
rows.english: Are you sure I learned it?

rows.medi_said: Would you say أنا كامل نسيت-- نسيتو؟ ... can you say كامل نسيتو؟ like completely forgot.
rows.why: He used كامل (whole/complete, an adjective) for the adverb 'completely'; Amal said لا and gave كليًا (sheet: completely / fully | Kulliyyan | كليًا).

rows.medi_said: The مرجة emotions. مرجة. Hold on. مرجة is for ... for future. right?
rows.why: Amal said لما نراجع الـ emotions (04:05, 04:15); he heard a non-word مرجة and took it for a future marker; she said No (04:26) and spelled out نراجع / مراجعة (04:28, 04:55). A word he had learned (she: 'Yes you did, أنا براجع' 05:09) that he did not recognise - listening, not his own production.
rows.r3_why: Transcript supports r1 exactly: his wrong hearing, her explicit No and the right word are all voiced. Listening row, tier 1 (a non-word).

rows.medi_said: فضاء means space, right?
rows.why: Amal asked اليوم في أي فصل؟ (05:44, 05:53); he heard فصل (season) as فضاء and glossed it 'space'; she repeated فصل (06:00) and he got it ('Oh yeah, فصل season' 06:01). Listening only.
rows.r3_why: He glossed what he heard as 'space', so he really heard فضاء; she repeated the word and he got it at once. Real listening mishear, voiced fix.

rows.medi_said: No, ربيع is spring. And then صيف is summer. شتاء is winter. Uh, let's see.
rows.chat: el-yoam yoam el-tenain ... awal yoam fi fasel el-5areef
rows.why: He listed the other three seasons and stalled on autumn; Amal supplied خريف and he said 'That's right' - a didn't-know (sheet: autumn / fall | 5areef).

rows.medi_said: بنطلون خضرا،
rows.chat: el-yoam balbes bluze soda u ban6aloan a5dar faate7 u kundara soda
rows.why: بنطلون is masculine; he gave the feminine colour خضرا and Amal recast أخضر, which he repeated.

rows.medi_said: عندهم
rows.why: He meant 'we have (about thirty days)' but put the they-ending on عند; Amal recast عنا and he fixed to عندنا.

rows.medi_said: حوالي تلاتين أيام.
rows.why: Numbers above ten take a singular noun; Amal repeated تلاتين to prompt, he said يوم, and she named the rule بعد العشرة يوم.

rows.medi_said: نحتاج، um, jacket.
rows.amal_said: آه، يعني نحتاج الـ jacket إندم.
rows.why: English jacket inside an Arabic sentence; her sheet has it (jacket | Jakait | جاكيت). Amal let it pass and used jacket herself - pre-ruled 'ok to switch', not scored.

rows.medi_said: بتغير.
rows.why: Subject is the thirty days (they); he used the singular بتغير, Amal prompted in English 'They change' and he produced بتغيروا.

rows.medi_said: أكلت الـ pizza ضل آآآ الـ آخر الأسبوع.
rows.amal_said: The pizza that remained. That remained from أخر الأسبوع. ... الـ pizza اللي remained
rows.chat: akalet el-pizza illi dallat min 2aa5er el-usboo3
rows.why: The relative 'that' (اللي) was missing before the verb; Amal prompted 'the pizza THAT remained' twice and he produced الـ pizza اللي at 14:39.
rows.english: I ate the pizza that was left from the weekend

rows.medi_said: أكلت الـ pizza ضل آآآ الـ آخر الأسبوع.
rows.amal_said: Mm، mm. The pizza that remained. That remained from أخر الأسبوع.
rows.why: Idafa: the first word never takes el-; he said الـ آخر الأسبوع (12:56) and again من الأخر الأسبوع (15:00, D4 folded here). Amal's 13:00 line was about اللي (A11) - her English gloss carried the bare أخر الأسبوع and she typed min 2aa5er el-usboo3 (15:41), but she never pointed at the el-, so B. Medium: the form is clear twice.
rows.english: the pizza that was left from the end of the week
rows.r3_why: Real A2 slip, twice; her voiced line fixed اللي, not this, and the typed line alone is not a correction (GR-19) - grammar-B. First occurrence, D4 is its repeat.

rows.medi_said: عادة مدينتي آآآ هادي، بس
rows.why: مدينة is feminine so the adjective is هادية; not voiced (she was listening to the sirens) - my reading.

rows.medi_said: لما / إشي بيصير / كل الـ fire department و ambulance آآآ آجوا.
rows.why: After لما the verb loses its b- (لما يصير إشي); he kept بيصير (14:12-14:16). Amal's only fix in this sentence was آجوا -> بيجو (A68, 14:29); she did not react to بيصير. My reading.
rows.english: when something happens, the whole fire department comes
rows.r3_why: Clear B3 slip in the transcript (the ب is written), let pass - grammar-B.

rows.medi_said: كل الـ fire department و ambulance آآآ آجوا.
rows.why: Habitual present ('they all come') needs the b- present; he used the past آجوا, Amal recast بيجو.

rows.medi_said: so الـ pizza اللي دلوا ... دل، دل.
rows.amal_said: One piece. Pizza is one. ... Pizza is woman. It's a, it's a feminine.
rows.why: He put a plural ending (دلوا) then bare دل on the verb for one feminine pizza (and ضل at 12:53); Amal prompted 'one piece ... feminine' until he said دلت / ضلت.

rows.medi_said: آآآ عشان جايبة لي pizza. ... دائمًا جايبة لي pizza.
rows.why: Answering her 'كان جاي على بالك pizza؟' (15:48, 16:02) he produced جايبة لي (bringing me) twice (16:22, 16:27); she laughed and recast كان جاي على بالك (16:26) and he fixed to 'ع بالي، جاي ع بالي pizza' (16:30). A mangled form of an expression on her sheet (i feel like / in the mood for | Jaay 3ala bali | جاي على بالي) - tier 2; medium because the engine can hear jaay 3abaali as jaayba li (sheet also lists Jaay 3abaali).
rows.r3_why: Both readers saw the same slip; tier is the only difference. He knows the expression (on the sheet) and garbled its shape, which is 'wrong form of a word he knows' = tier 2, not a different lexical item. Her laugh + recast and his immediate fix are voiced.

rows.medi_said: آآآ أنا ما بحب الـ، الفلفل حلو ... حلو
rows.amal_said: ولا أنا ما بحب الحلو. بحب البحري. ما بحب الفلفل الحلو.
rows.why: Noun + adjective as one thing needs el- on both (الفلفل الحلو); الفلفل حلو reads as 'the pepper is sweet'. Amal recast ما بحب الفلفل الحلو. He then said الـ فلفل بهري (18:06) with the same gap.

rows.medi_said: نشاف or yeah نشاف؟
rows.why: Wrong form of a word he knows (sheet: dry | Naashef | ناشف); Amal recast ناشف and he repeated it.

rows.medi_said: So if you ask for a pastry, do you say واحد حلو؟ حلوة؟ أو وحدة حلوة؟ ... something sweet like a pastry.
rows.amal_said: يعني كعكة. ... بسكوتة، كعكة، خلص احكي Pastry.
rows.why: He asked how to ask for a pastry; Amal supplied كعكة / بسكوتة - a didn't-know.

rows.medi_said: So تستانا is to order or, or an order?
rows.why: He did not recognise تستنى (wait; sheet wait | estanna) in her line and guessed 'order'; she repeated it and he worked out 'sit and wait'. Listening.

rows.medi_said: شكرًا. سلامة إيديكي
rows.why: The thank-you phrase is يسلمو إيديكي (sheet: thanks | yeslamu); he built it with سلامة. Amal moved on to the price - my reading.

rows.medi_said: uh, أديش الحق؟
rows.why: 'How much is it' needs the owner ending on حق (حقها), not el-; Amal prompted 'its price' and he moved to حقو then حقها.

rows.medi_said: أديش حقو؟
rows.why: قهوة is feminine so the ending is -ha; he used -o and Amal recast حقها 'cuz it's coffee'; he repeated حقها.

rows.medi_said: uh, رح / بقدر / أد-أدفع
rows.why: After رح the verb loses its b-; he said رح بقدر. Amal's chat has only ba2dar; no voiced signal.
rows.english: I will be able to pay

rows.medi_said: أدفع أطفالهم (engine; he said أدفع لهم) ... Do I still need to say أدفع لهم؟ ... Pay for them no?
rows.amal_said: لا. ... أدفع عن. Pay for. Like you pay for me for example. بدفع عنك.
rows.right: أدفع عنهم / just أدفع بالـ credit card
rows.why: He used دفع لـ to mean 'pay for (the items)'; Amal said لا and named the pairing: pay for = أدفع عن, pay to someone = أدفع لـ. Engine wrote أطفالهم for لهم.

rows.medi_said: أدفع أطفالهم مع credit card مع... uh, من؟
rows.amal_said: أدفع. You use the credit card to pay. So what do you use? Which preposition? ... B. Credit card.
rows.why: Paying 'with' a card takes بـ, not مع; Amal asked which preposition, gave 'B', and he produced أدفع بالـ credit card.

rows.medi_said: Or it's feminine. هذا الأكلة.
rows.amal_said: You were right هذي الأكلة. هذي is for feminine.
rows.why: He first said هادي then switched to هذا; أكلة is feminine, Amal named the rule and he took هذي.

rows.medi_said: مش طازة. و... مش زاكي.
rows.chat: haadi el-akle mish taaza u mish zaakye
rows.why: أكلة is feminine so the adjective is زاكية; Amal only typed zaakye. طازة is m/f on her sheet so only زاكي is off - my reading.
rows.english: it is not fresh and not tasty

rows.medi_said: Or how do I say something's wrong with it? Is she, is she غلط مايك or-- does that make sense ... إشي، إشي غلط بـ... In it? ... And it would be فيه or
rows.amal_said: You would say in it or there's something wrong with it or in it. ... In it. ... فيها. ... أو فيها إشي غلط.
rows.why: He asked 'how do I say something's wrong with it?' (29:03) and tried غلط مايك / غلط بـ; Amal prompted 'in it' in English (29:16, 29:28), he asked 'فيه or' (29:34) and she supplied فيها (29:37) then the whole phrase فيها إشي غلط (29:40), which he repeated (29:43). One didn't-know moment built with her; his 'فيه or' was a question about the gender, not a use.
rows.english: there is something wrong with it (the dish)
rows.r3_why: Same moment in both readers; the transcript shows it opened as 'how do I say X?' and she built the phrase with him step by step, so it is a didn't-know (tier 0, asked), not a scored D3 grammar slip - his فيه came as a question ('فيه or'), which is neither a slip nor a use.

rows.medi_said: أستاذ. / ما بعرف
rows.amal_said: It's like sir. We learned it.
rows.why: Listening: she asked شو يعني أستاذ, he said ما بعرف; she explained 'sir' (sheet: professor / teacher | Ustaaz | أستاز).

rows.medi_said: The north? ... Shumel. Shumen. Men is...
rows.amal_said: شو مال الشاورما؟ ... It's like شو مالك؟ شو مالك؟ شو مال الشاورما؟
rows.why: Amal asked شو مالها الشاورما؟ (31:18, 31:26); he heard it as شمال and guessed 'The north?' (31:24, 31:29); she repeated and explained شو مالك / شو مال الشاورما (31:37) and he got 'what's wrong with the' (31:39). A wrong word for what he heard (not a 'how do you say' question) - tier 1, listening.
rows.r3_why: Both readers agree on the row; tier differs. He supplied a wrong word (north) rather than asking for a word, so tier 1 like D1/D2/D21, not tier 0.

rows.medi_said: طعم، uh, طعمها مرة و حامضة
rows.amal_said: خلص إنت هلأ you're now describing the taste so it's more (مر).
rows.why: He made the adjectives agree with the feminine أكلة, but the subject is طعم (masc.); Amal corrected in English ('describing the taste so it's murr') and typed murr u haamed; he repeated 'tam mur oo hamid'.
rows.english: its taste is bitter and sour

rows.medi_said: أول مرة؟ ... بيهنّا. Should-- Wait, oh, بيهنّا. ... Is بيهم important, like مهم؟
rows.amal_said: إحنا بيهمنا زبايننا يكونوا مبسوطين. شو يعني؟ ... بهم، بيهمنا. ... It matters to us.
rows.why: She asked شو يعني؟ of her own إحنا بيهمنا زبايننا (34:01); he could not say (أول مرة؟ 34:07), echoed بيهنّا (34:12), she repeated بهم، بيهمنا (34:15) and glossed 'It matters to us' (34:30) after he guessed 'Is بيهم important, like مهم؟'. Listening / didn't-know of a sheet word (it matters | Beyhemm | بيهم).
rows.english: we care that our customers are happy
rows.r3_why: Transcript supports r2: she asked the meaning, he did not have it, she supplied it - tier 0 asked, listening.

rows.medi_said: ana ma-ana maruf, ana-- akun ana maruf.
rows.why: Plain present needs no 'to be'; he added أكون to 'I am known'. Amal typed ana ma3roof - my reading.

rows.medi_said: would it be a-ana mash-mashhur bi-ut-bi atbuk without the bi, right?
rows.amal_said: في. في or be. في، mm, the noun. Noun is طبخ.
rows.why: After bi / fi the noun of the action goes, not a verb; Amal said 'the noun is طبخ' and he produced bi طبخ الكباب (38:29).
rows.english: I am famous for cooking kebab

rows.medi_said: أنا بظن إنه هادي مش لازم ... Makan,
rows.amal_said: مش لا-- إنه ما كان لازم، صح.
rows.chat: bas ana bazonn enno ma kaan laazem
rows.why: 'It wasn't necessary' (past) needs كان stacked on لازم and the ما negation; he said مش لازم, started 'Makan' as she recast ما كان لازم, and he repeated it.
rows.english: I think it wasn't necessary (to wash the rice)

rows.medi_said: uh, is not, yeah, mish il-roz fi Iran.
rows.chat: el-ruzz hoan mish zayy el-ruzz bi Iran
rows.why: 'The rice here is not LIKE the rice in Iran' needs the preposition زي; he left it out (40:17-40:22), Amal prompted 'مش it's not like' (40:25) and he produced مش، زي / mish zay il-roz bi Iran (40:27, 40:32). A missing small word, not a wrong lexical item - prepositions D1 (sheet: like | zayy | زي).
rows.english: the rice here is not like the rice in Iran
rows.r3_why: Same slip in both readers; kind differs. Nothing was substituted - a preposition was missing and her prompt added it, which is grammar D1 rather than a vocab tier-1 wrong word.

rows.medi_said: Bi, bibi'u, ishna bibi'?
rows.why: الشركة is feminine so the verb takes بت-; he groped بي-, Amal gave بتبيع 'because شركة is...' and he said 'Yeah, feminine. بتبيع الرز'.

rows.medi_said: Yeah, feminine. بتبيع بتبيع الرز uh,
rows.why: Inside الشركة اللي ... about the rice already under discussion (الرز هون 40:17) the object rides on the verb as a pronoun (بتبيعه); he repeated the full noun and Amal recast بتبيعه (41:09), typed betbi3o. Endings-on-verbs D4; the pointing-back use of the ending is C2 (bucket2).
rows.english: the company that sells it (the rice)
rows.r3_why: Both readers agree on the slip; only the bucket differs. The fix is a pronoun ending on the verb (D4); the rice was not fronted inside this sentence, so C2 is secondary.

rows.medi_said: بيغسل الـ
